trace.answer:
Unemployment in Kitchener-Cambridge-Waterloo is higher now than in 2019, though well below the pandemic peak.

- **2019 baseline:** The monthly rate ran between 4.8% and 5.5%, averaging about 5.2%.
- **Pandemic spike:** It rose sharply in spring 2020 and peaked at 13.1% in June and July 2020.
- **Recovery to 2022:** It fell back to about 5.3% by late 2021 and early 2022, then rose to about 6% through 2022.
- **2023:** It moved between 5.6% and 6.3%.
- **2024 onward:** It climbed steadily from about 6.2% in April 2024 to 8.0% by October 2024, and stayed around 7.2% to 8.1% through 2025.
- **2026:** It reached 9.0% in April 2026, the highest since the pandemic peak, then eased to 7.7% in September 2026, the latest month available.

So the September 2026 rate of 7.7% is about 2.2 percentage points above September 2019 (5.5%).

These are seasonally adjusted, three-month moving averages for the Kitchener-Cambridge-Waterloo census metropolitan area, so single-month changes are smoothed and may be revised.

Source: Statistics Canada, Table 14-10-0459-01, *Labour force characteristics by census metropolitan area, three-month moving average, seasonally adjusted* (DOI: https://doi.org/10.25318/1410045901-eng). I found no Ontario government dataset specifically about minimum wage. Two searches of the Ontario catalogue (data.ontario.ca), one for "Ontario minimum wage" and one for "Employment Standards Act minimum wage rates", returned nothing on the topic.

The closest federal dataset is one that covers Canada as a whole:

- **Historical minimum wage rates in Canada** (Employment and Social Development Canada). It is a CSV dataset that describes the minimum wage as a basic labour standard, and it was last modified 2026-10-04. Its two CSV resources are queryable. Ontario is very likely included, since the dataset covers the country, but I could not confirm that. A preview attempt failed with an internal error, so I have not checked its contents. Licence: Open Government Licence – Canada. Page: https://open.canada.ca/data/en/dataset/390ee890-59bb-4f34-a37c-9732781ef8a0

Other results that may be relevant:

- **Current and forthcoming minimum hourly wage for adult and young workers** (federal). The data table has been removed, and the page points to the Government of Canada's Minimum Wage Database: https://srv116.services.gc.ca/dimt-wid/sm-mw/menu.aspx?GoCTemplateCulture=en-CA. This is probably the best current source for Ontario's rate, but I have not checked the database itself.
- **Nova Scotia Minimum Wage** (provincial, not Ontario). It is a CSV dataset last modified 2026-04-17, licensed under the Open Government Licence – Canada.

The Ontario wage datasets returned by the search (for example "Wage rates by occupation" and "Wages rates by industry") are general wage statistics rather than minimum wage data. They were last updated in 2021.

If you want, I can retry the federal historical dataset to check whether it includes Ontario rows.
